summary: Prove that the packed package installs and runs on a clean consumer, then bind release checks, a package-scoped CycloneDX SBOM, and cross-platform tests to the exact artifact. Keep publication blocked until bundled-content rights and an allowlisted signing fingerprint are verified, and document the guards' security limits.
plain_summary: New users can install the tool from a clean device; maintainers can release only a tested, attributable package and explain its security limits.
gating: Plan approved on 2026-11-05. Work checkpoints in order. Within each checkpoint, behavior runs before UI, then review. A checkpoint passes only when every gate is passed or n/a. Do not start checkpoint N+1 until checkpoint N has passed.

checkpoints.title: Prove the packed package runs
checkpoints.goal: The exact packed tarball installs in an isolated consumer and `ai-eng --version` succeeds under Bun without Node.

plain.what: A first-time user can install the package and see the tool start from a clean folder.
plain.why: A broken launcher or omitted file stops every new user before their first command.
plain.check: Install the packed file in a clean folder, then ask the tool to show its version.

tasks: Change bin/ai-eng.js so the installed command starts with Bun, while preserving the npm-install path and the clear refusal when Bun is unavailable.
Add a package-consumer smoke procedure that creates and installs the actual npm tarball in a fresh consumer; include a Bun-only PATH case that cannot find Node.
Test the installed consumer's exact version output and exit status, the launcher entry point, and the files actually present in the tarball rather than inspecting only the checkout.
Keep TOML parsing on Bun.TOML; do not add smol-toml or another runtime dependency.
acceptance: A tarball produced from the checkout installs in a clean npm consumer and its installed ai-eng command reports the package version successfully.
The installed command also runs with Bun available and Node absent; a missing Bun runtime returns a clear nonzero refusal rather than a stack trace.
Assertions cover exact consumer output and the complete relevant packed-file contents, not source-string presence.
No smol-toml runtime import or new dependency is introduced.

findings: Focused 14/14, lint, typecheck, build green. Full serial suite 1747 pass / 16 skip / 1 fail: pre-existing artifact-scroll-spy failure from the approved brainstorm's minified script (on main since 40a18cab); fixed in 214adac5, scroll-spy 4/4.

Round 3 PASS: dev-checkout and dist ordering pinned under bun (launcher.spec.ts:261, :272); npm-manifest uses the Windows-aware runner. Behavior re-run after fixes: focused 23/23, suite 1757 pass / 16 skip / 0 fail, lint, typecheck, build green.
Earlier rounds: dist/-dependent tests (L252), bun path untested (L253) — fixed.

checkpoints.title: Run the full suite on every platform
checkpoints.goal: The complete serial Bun suite and existing platform smoke checks pass on Linux, macOS, and Windows, including receipt-retention coverage.

plain.what: Maintainers see the complete checks pass on Linux, macOS, and Windows.
plain.why: A green result on one computer cannot show that every supported user is covered.
plain.check: Read three separate system results, each showing the same complete checks passed.

tasks: Extend .github/workflows/platforms.yml so each supported operating-system job runs bun test --parallel=1 in addition to the existing init, doctor, uninstall, and build checks.
Reproduce and retain the first receipt-retention timeout's test, assertion, and environment before changing it; fix its cause without hiding failures or weakening its behavior assertions.
Keep retention bounded and correct under the existing batch, concurrency, and late-arrival cases; use the receipt-retention lessons in LEARNINGS.md rather than relaxing its limits.
acceptance: Linux, macOS, and Windows each run the full serial suite and preserve the existing platform smoke checks.
The receipt-retention timeout is reproducibly resolved on the affected runner without removing assertions, skipping failures, increasing a performance budget, or masking the first failure.
Retention still deletes only the intended stale batch and preserves young receipts, late arrivals, and single-claim concurrency behavior.

checkpoints.title: Bind release proof to the packed SHA
checkpoints.goal: Release checks and build inputs use the exact dispatched SHA, and the same packed tarball is smoke-tested, represented by a licensed runtime-only CycloneDX SBOM, and published.

plain.what: The package people receive is the same one maintainers tested and described.
plain.why: Testing a nearby copy cannot prove what a release actually contains.
plain.check: Compare the tested package and its inventory with the package named in the release.

tasks: Add a release verification job in .github/workflows/release.yml that checks out and asserts the exact workflow-dispatch SHA, then runs lint, typecheck, the serial full suite, and build before any release build or publication job.
Pack once from that verified SHA, retain the tarball and its digest as an artifact, run the checkpoint-1 clean-consumer smoke against that exact file, and publish that same tarball without repacking.

Generate CycloneDX from the installed tarball's runtime dependency graph, not the repository root; include the package and runtime transitive components, exclude development-only dependencies, and fail if any component lacks license metadata.
Attach the package-scoped SBOM and its checksum/provenance with the release artifacts; preserve the existing version/channel checks.
acceptance: The verification job proves its checkout SHA equals the dispatched SHA; checks finish successfully before release builds and before any registry or GitHub publication mutation.
The smoke test, SBOM, and npm publication all name the same tarball digest produced from that SHA; the workflow does not repack during publication.
The CycloneDX SBOM describes the installed package's runtime dependency graph and contains license metadata for every included component; missing metadata blocks release.
The SBOM is not repository-wide and does not include development-only dependencies.

checkpoints.title: Require verified signing and rights before release
checkpoints.goal: Every future publication requires an annotated tag signed by an owner-configured allowlisted fingerprint and verified redistribution rights for all bundled content; user documentation states the guard boundary accurately.

plain.what: People can see who approved a release and what the tool can and cannot protect.
plain.why: An unknown signer or unresolved content rights must never be treated as permission to publish.
plain.check: Confirm an unapproved release stops and the guide explains when extra isolation is needed.

tasks: Add a release-policy check that requires an existing annotated, cryptographically signed tag and verifies its signer against a configured allowlisted fingerprint before either npm or GitHub publication.
Fail closed when the signer fingerprint is absent, malformed, or does not match; do not supply, guess, or commit an authorized fingerprint. Keep tag 2.6.0 unchanged.

Gate every publication channel while any bundled content lacks owner-verified redistribution rights. Keep the existing unresolved attribution entries as blockers; do not invent licenses, claim permission, or delete content.

Test refusal before publication for unresolved rights, missing or untrusted signer configuration, unannotated tags, and invalid signatures, plus a controlled fixture where all required evidence is supplied.

Update README.md to say that the Copilot CLI adapter can fail open and that command guards do not sandbox opaque programs or scripts prepared in earlier calls; recommend OS-level isolation for untrusted code.
acceptance: Before any publish step, future tags must be annotated, cryptographically verified, and signed by the exact configured allowlisted fingerprint; missing or mismatched configuration refuses publication.
Both release channels remain blocked while any bundled content has unresolved redistribution rights, including the currently documented H4 items; tests cannot silently resolve those facts.
No rights, license, or signer identity is invented, and no existing tag—especially 2.6.0—is rewritten.
README.md accurately explains Copilot fail-open behavior, the lack of OS sandboxing, and the need for OS-level isolation when running untrusted code.

assumptions: Bun remains the supported runtime, and the built-in TOML parser remains in use [approved production-readiness brainstorm; package.json and src].
No signing fingerprint or redistribution right is inferred; an authorized owner must supply and verify each fact [approved brainstorm; current NOTICE.md and THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.md].
The published 2.6.0 tag and all remote release state remain unchanged [approved brainstorm].
notes: The allowlisted signer fingerprint and proof of redistribution rights are unresolved owner-controlled blockers; publication stays disabled until both are verified.
Do not rewrite tag 2.6.0, publish, push, or dispatch remote workflows.
